transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-21
Start time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), John Ramirez (CTO - New Windsor), Maria Santos (Infra Lead), Kevin O'Neill (Security), Sara Liu (Network), Tom Park (DevOps)

Summary: quick intake to map New Windsor's private onramp needs. Primary asks: region gating (EU-only), private endpoints vs. transit-gw peering, egress IP stability, KMS/HSM for encryption, and a short Dedicated trial to validate latency/throughput.

Topics: networking topology, private endpoints, transit gateway vs VPC peering, egress IPs/NAT, region restrictions (eu-west-1 + uk-south), audit/logging, pilot plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. testing audio ok?
[00:12] John Ramirez: yeah, can hear you — cheers.
[00:15] Priya Kapoor: great, i'll just run the agenda quick — intake on network, compliance needs, pilot timeline, then next steps.
[00:23] Maria Santos: cool, we've got limited time so i'll be concise. our primary constraint is data residency — must keep inference traffic and model state inside EU (eu-west-1 + maybe london region). also want private-only access, no public internet endpoints.
[00:40] Alex Chen: understood. so you're looking at Redwood Private in a VPC-mode, correct? not hosted API.
[00:48] John Ramirez: yes. we evaluated hosted but the auditors flagged data exfil risk. we'd consider Dedicated if it helps with latency and isolation.
[00:57] Priya Kapoor: ok, two common patterns — private endpoints (PrivateLink style) or transit gateway peering to our VPCs. each has tradeoffs: PrivateLink gives per-subnet ENIs and stable private DNS, transit-gw is better for many-VPC architectures and reduces per-endpoint plumbing. do you currently run transit gateway?
[01:18] Sara Liu: yes, we use TGW across 4 VPCs and two accounts; also have a shared services VPC. we prefer centralized egress through NAT GW in a single egress VPC to keep IPs stable.
[01:30] Tom Park: and the egress IPs are important because our security rules only allow a handful of partner IPs.
[01:36] Priya Kapoor: ok, that maps well to a transit-gw approach with an egress VPC. Redwood can expose private endpoints in the customer VPC or accept traffic over a transit attachment. a couple details to confirm: do you need TLS termination on your side or shall we terminate at our side and present a private endpoint with mTLS?
[01:56] Kevin O'Neill: security preference is mTLS mutual auth, and we'd like HSM-backed KMS for keys. also need full audit logs for prompt content retention policy (we may redact later) — what are the retention controls?
[02:12] Alex Chen: we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations in Private deployments. audit logs are available; retention can be configured but we'll share our security whitepaper. note: prompts can be optionally disabled from retention or redacted via redaction hooks, but that's part of the config during onboarding.
[02:30] John Ramirez: good. on region gating — if we pin to eu-west-1, can Redwood guarantee compute lives in that region for Private?
[02:41] Priya Kapoor: yes, Private deployment can be pinned to specific regions. Dedicated can reserve capacity in eu-west-1. the only caveat is model variants that require specialized hw — we'll surface compatible variants limited to that region.
[02:56] Maria Santos: whats the networking topology you recommend for low latency between our app tier and the model endpoints? we have an app VPC in eu-west-1 too.
[03:07] Priya Kapoor: shortest path is private endpoint in the same region VPC, ideally in the same AZ to avoid cross-AZ hops. if you want centralization for many VPCs, use TGW with route propagation. also consider pinned subnets and placement groups on our side; we'll share a diagram.
[03:25] Sara Liu: any MTU or fragmentation issues we should know about? we already have jumbo frames internally.
[03:31] Priya Kapoor: we typically support standard MTU 1500; jumbo can be supported but must be negotiated because the service ENIs are 1500 default. we'll note that as an action item.
[03:42] Tom Park: about egress: we push outbound calls through a NAT GW with a fixed set of Elastic IPs. can Redwood allow us to present those as allowed egress for callbacks and model downloads?
[03:55] Alex Chen: Redwood's Private nodes can be configured to use customer egress via NAT. But for hosted fallback or external artifact pulls, we may need to route in/out — we can document the exact egress IP set and you can whitelist them. for Dedicated, that list is smaller and more stable.
[04:14] John Ramirez: what about bringing your runtime on-prem? we have a colo in FRA that houses some latency-sensitive services.
[04:23] Priya Kapoor: we do private on-prem packages but it's heavier. two options: run Redwood Private in the cloud with a private interconnect (Direct Connect or ExpressRoute) back to colocation, or an on-prem bundle — both need network workshop. colo needs certain kernel/driver support for GPUs.
[04:40] Maria Santos: our preference is cloud VPC + direct connect — simpler from ops.
[04:44] Kevin O'Neill: compliance question: do you support customer-managed logging to our S3 and meet GDPR deletion requests?
[04:51] Alex Chen: yes, we can forward audit logs to your S3, and we support deletion workflows tied to records. exact SLA for deletion depends on deployment type; we'll include it in the security doc.
[05:03] Priya Kapoor: quick question — how many QPS and token/sec are you expecting for the pilot?
[05:10] John Ramirez: pilot is small — maybe 5-10 rps, peak 60 concurrent requests, median prompt length ~120 tokens, embedding calls lower but continuous. aim is to simulate production with a 2-week burst.
[05:25] Priya Kapoor: cool, that's modest. Dedicated trial will let us reserve a small pool and test cold-starts and KV cache behavior. we can also enable prefix caching to reduce token cost.
[05:36] Tom Park: is prefix caching automatic? how does it handle user prompt variations?
[05:41] Priya Kapoor: its workload-aware; similar prefixes are cached, but it's not semantic — exact token prefixes or KV cache from previous contexts. for chat-like sessions you'll see big benefits.
[05:51] Sara Liu: about endpoint types — PrivateLink vs Private NLB in peered VPC — any recommendations given our TGW architecture?
[06:00] Priya Kapoor: if you prefer minimal route table changes and per-account isolation, use PrivateLink. If you have TGW and want multicast-like access across many VPCs, an NLB + TGW attachment could be simpler. PrivateLink has more ENI overhead.
[06:15] Maria Santos: any cost differences we should be aware of?
[06:18] Alex Chen: PrivateLink has per-GB and per-hour ENI costs on AWS; TGW attachments are charged differently. We'll include rough cost delta in the follow-up. Dedicated pricing vs PrivateLink tradeoffs we'll outline.
[06:30] Kevin O'Neill: what about IP allowlists — can we do client cert pinning or are IPs the only primitive?
[06:36] Priya Kapoor: we support mTLS, and we can do per-token level RBAC as well. For IP allowlists, we provide a fixed set for Dedicated; for hosted it's larger. We'll provide the list.
[06:47] John Ramirez: network ACLs — we want to restrict egress to only certain S3 buckets for model weights. is there a way to ensure downloads only happen from your signed buckets?
[06:58] Alex Chen: yes, we can sign artifact URLs and optionally host model weights in your S3 via replication. there's a secure artifact fetch flow; we'll show the sequence diagram.
[07:09] Sara Liu: latency question — what's typical RTT for eu-west-1 in a dedicated deployment?
[07:15] Priya Kapoor: cold start time depends on model and quantization. For a 13B model with fast kernels in our runtime, token latency is ~25–45ms steady-state when co-located in same AZ. We'll include benchmark numbers.
[07:29] Tom Park: if we pin model quantization (int8) does that change the network requirements?
[07:34] Priya Kapoor: mostly affects compute, not networking. smaller memory footprint may reduce cache spills but networking same.
[07:41] Maria Santos: regarding DNS, we use split-horizon internal DNS. can your private endpoints honor our internal DNS names?
[07:48] Alex Chen: yes, via private hosted zones and endpoint DNS configuration we can map service names to private IPs. we'll include DNS config notes.
[07:58] John Ramirez: ok, let's talk failure modes — if your cluster in eu-west-1 is overloaded, do you fail open to hosted multi-region? we can't allow cross-border failover automatically.
[08:11] Priya Kapoor: we have routing policies: you can set strict region-only or allow automatic fallback to a designated region. given your compliance constraints, we'd set strict region-only and then configure on-call alerts and capacity escalation. fallback to other region would be manual and requires your sign-off.
[08:29] Kevin O'Neill: are there SLA credits tied to latency or availability?
[08:33] Alex Chen: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency tiers. Private (on prem) gets enterprise SLAs — we'll include the doc.
[08:42] Maria Santos: network path MTU — you mentioned default 1500. we use 9001 internally. can the Redwood ENIs be jumbo-aware?
[08:51] Priya Kapoor: it's not enabled by default. we can work with AWS settings but it's a multi-party change; we'll put that in the workshop.
[08:58] Tom Park: who on Redwood will run the network workshop?
[09:02] Alex Chen: Priya will lead the technical side; i'll coordinate logistics and pricing items.
[09:07] Priya Kapoor: action item list — i'll collect your TGW attachments, route tables, and NAT EIP list. also we'll sketch two proposed topologies: PrivateLink and TGW+NLB.
[09:18] John Ramirez: sounds good. timeline — we'd like pilot running early Jan; is that realistic?
[09:23] Alex Chen: yes — if we get your infra details by Jan 4 we can spin a minimal Dedicated trial the week of Jan 9.
[09:30] Maria Santos: one more — audit and redaction. we have legal asking for selective prompt redaction before any log leaves region. can Redwood do inline redaction?
[09:40] Priya Kapoor: yes, we have redaction hooks that run pre-ingest; they can be customer-provided regex or a server-side plugin. performance impact is minimal but we should test it in pilot.
[09:51] Kevin O'Neill: encryption in transit — do you support TLS 1.3?
[09:54] Alex Chen: yes, TLS 1.3 supported and mTLS for private endpoints.
[09:59] Sara Liu: regarding IPs again — we want the smallest possible allowlist. for dedicated trial what's the size?
[10:05] Priya Kapoor: dedicated trial can give you a /28-ish stable set depending on deployment; we'll confirm exact count.
[10:12] Tom Park: can we get a sample Terraform module for peering + route table changes?
[10:18] Alex Chen: yes, we'll attach a starter TF module and routing snippets.
[10:22] John Ramirez: any blockers from our side? we need to validate budget and schedule security review.
[10:28] Alex Chen: understood. we'll send pricing bands and the SOC2/ISO docs.
[10:32] Maria Santos: ok thanks. let's capture the follow-ups.
[10:36] Alex Chen: recap: Priya will run network workshop early Jan; Alex to send diagrams, pricing, security docs; customer to provide CIDRs, TGW attachments, NAT EIPs by Jan 4. Dedicated trial proposed week of Jan 9.
[10:52] John Ramirez: perfect, appreciate it.
[10:55] Kevin O'Neill: thanks all.
[10:58] Alex Chen: thanks everyone, talk soon. bye.

Note: transcript contains natural filler, occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "multicast-like access" used colloquially), and some proper nouns slightly garbled.
